messages:
sasha: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need to pick a single resume/cursor story that maps cleanly to Python generators, TS AsyncIterator, and Go channels. Current proposals are diverging (opaque resume token vs server-offset + page cursor). Thoughts?
kevin: tl;dr: prefer opaque resume token + explicit page boundary. language ergonomics map well if token is small and stable.
taylor: Agree on opaque token but want to call out retries. If token is opaque, how do we make retries idempotent across pages?
sasha: Good call. My proposal: each request includes a client-generated idempotency key for mutation-style endpoints. For read/paginate endpoints we return a resume token that is deterministic for the page boundary so re-requesting the same page is safe.
alex: Example shapes? would help.
sasha: Sure — response shape idea:```json
{
  "items": [...],
  "next_resume_token": "r:eyJvZmZz...",
  "page_stable_at": "2025-04-01T14:22:00Z"
}
```
And the client usage patterns: Python generator consumes pages and yields items; if a page fails, we can retry with the same `next_resume_token`.
kevin: In TS AsyncIterator we'd do `for await (const item of client.list())` under the hood it would fetch pages and buffer items. Resume token fits that model.
maya: In Go channels the ergonomic pattern is `ch := client.List(ctx, opts)` then `for it := range ch { ... }`. If we make `next_resume_token` opaque bytes, Go lib should expose a helper `ResumeFrom(token string)` to reconstruct channel state.
taylor: Two concerns: 1) token lifetime (short-lived server-side cursor vs permanent bookmark). 2) cross-version compatibility (models/serialization changes).
sasha: For 1, server should encode expiry inside the token and return TTL header. For 2, recommend token be versioned: `v1:<base64>` so we can rotate. Also guarantee forward-compat: newer server should reject unknown versions with 4xx and provide migration hint.
alex: What about streaming transports (gRPC or Websocket) vs unary HTTP pages? Resume semantics differ — streaming can stream an ever-growing timeline where resume token is just last-seen offset.
kevin: We should keep a single surface but different transport adapters. For streaming: emit checkpoints (opaque offsets) on punctuated intervals. For paging/unary: next_resume_token as above. Expose the same SDK API so callers don't need to know transport.
taylor: Retries: we need to coordinate retry windows and backoff with pagination because re-requesting a page may re-run expensive backend work. Suggest server-side cheap checkpoints (KV cache) keyed on resume token to make retries cheap. Also doc: clients SHOULD not retry automatically more than N times for the same page unless caller opted in.
sasha: +1. Also recommend an SDK-level retry budget per-list-call that counts per-page retries separately from transport-level retries. E.g., overallBudget=3, perPageBudget=1.
maya: Ergonomics: provide helpers in each SDK: `ListOptions{resumeToken, pageSize, retryBudget}` or in TS `list({ resumeToken, pageSize, retryBudget })`. Keep surface consistent: same field names across langs.
alex: Edge case: APIs that modify resources mid-pagination (moving window) — a client might resume and see duplicates/missing items if the underlying dataset changed. How do we advise customers?
kevin: Docs: for mutable datasets, server must offer either snapshotting semantics per-list-call, or best-effort “consistent as of resume_token” with note about eventual consistency. Don't try to hide semantics behind token.
taylor: Implementation note for SDKs: Python generator should be lazy but expose `peek_resume()` helper to persist resume token during iteration. TS AsyncIterator could expose `iterator.resumeToken()` or a separate function `client.listStream().checkpoint()`. Go channel variant should return a small controller object `{C <-chan Item, Checkpoint() string}`.
sasha: Example UX (Python):```py
it = client.list_messages(page_size=100)
for msg in it:
    process(msg)
    if need_to_pause:
        token = it.peek_resume()
        save(token)
        break
```
TS:```ts
const it = client.listMessages({pageSize:100});
for await (const msg of it) {
  // same idea
  if (shouldPause) {
    const token = (it as any).checkpoint(); // helper on iterator
    save(token);
    break;
  }
}
```
Go:```go
ctrl := client.ListMessages(ctx, ListOpts{PageSize:100})
for msg := range ctrl.C {
  if pause {
    tok := ctrl.Checkpoint()
    save(tok)
    break
  }
}
```
kevin: We should also expose a low-level `ResumeFrom(token)` API that reconstructs iterator/channel for resumed consumption, returning the same types.
maya: Testing: include integration tests that simulate server-side token expiry and ensure client surfaces the right error so caller can re-query from scratch.
taylor: Security: tokens may leak info. Keep them scoped and opaque; avoid embedding raw resource ids. Use MACs or KMS-signed blobs.
sasha: Ops: add metrics for resume-token churn and invalid-token errors (per-API). That will help debug client migrations.
ci-bot: Reminder: RFC follow-up checklist created as ticket INF-1254.
alex: Decision summary proposal: 1) Use opaque, versioned resume tokens for both streaming checkpoints and paging. 2) Expose consistent API across languages with small helpers: `peek_resume`/`checkpoint`/`Checkpoint()` + `ResumeFrom(token)`. 3) Server includes TTL & version in token; server caches page checkpoints for efficient retries. 4) SDKs implement a per-call retry budget and surface retry controls. 5) Document mutation vs read semantics clearly.
kevin: :+1: from me, will draft the SDK stubs.
taylor: :+1: I'll add the retry budget wiring to the Python/TS runtime adapters.
maya: I'll sketch the Go controller API and a tiny migration guide for customers.
sasha: Thanks all — I'll post a short RFC update and wire INF-1254 to implementations.
ci-bot: Deploy pipeline: none.
